extracted.intended_audience: parties sued for patent infringement, patent owners, and IP attorneys considering or defending Covered Business Method (CBM) reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to initiate and defend a Covered Business Method (CBM) review before the PTAB, including eligibility, timing, grounds, procedural steps, and likely outcomes. Targeted at petitioners, patent owners, and counsel evaluating CBM as a post-grant challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Is A Covered Business Method?
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered Business Method (CBM) patents are methods, apparatuses, or operations used in the practice, administration or management of a financial product or service. CBM patents exclude “technological inventions,” which claim a novel and non-obvious technological feature that solves a technical problem using a technical solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether a challenged patent falls within the CBM class (financial product/service focus). Exclude patents that claim technological inventions that solve technical problems with technical solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A CBM review must be initiated within nine months of the issuance of the patent or the date of termination of a post-grant review, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM can be filed only when a post-grant review is unavailable (e.g., after the nine-month post-issuance window). Compare timing against post-grant review (PGR) windows when assessing which remedy to pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who May File / Standing
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file with the USPTO a petition to institute a covered business method patent review of a patent if the petitioner or the petitioner's real party-in-interest has been sued for infringement of the patent or has been charged with infringement under patent law. A petitioner must meet the exact standing requirements as if that petitioner were to file a declaratory judgment in Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner may not file for CBM review if (i) the petitioner or the petitioner's real party-in-interest has already filed a civil action challenging the validity of a patent claim, or (ii) the petitioner, the petitioner's real party-in-interest, or a privy of the petitioner is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified in the petition. Carefully evaluate prior litigation and estoppel risks before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Review / Invalidity Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must assert that at least one claim of the challenged patent is directed to a covered business method and that the claim is invalid under the statutory grounds of patentability, such as anticipation, obviousness, or lack of written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM challenges may be based on statutory bases including (as noted) 35 U.S.C. §101 (subject matter), §103 (obviousness), §112 (written description/enablement). Ensure the petition ties the asserted statutory grounds to the claim language and provides supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file a petition for CBM review with the PTAB, providing specific information about the challenged patent, the grounds for invalidity, and any supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a petition that includes identification of challenged claims, detailed explanations of grounds, citations to prior art/evidence, and any necessary declarations. Procedural compliance and completeness are essential for institution considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure (briefing, discovery, hearings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBM review process involves briefing, discovery, and possibly oral hearings, similar to other post-grant review proceedings. Both the petitioner and the patent owner have opportunities to present evidence and arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM discovery is broader than some other post-grant proceedings (see Discovery row). Plan for briefing schedules, potential depositions, document production, and the possibility of an oral hearing before the PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Evidence (scope and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior Art Evidence: All patents, publications, prior and products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally CBM proceedings may consider patents, publications, and prior products as prior art. For patents granted under the first-to-invent rules (filed prior to March 16, 2013), prior art available for CBM review may be limited by section 18(a)(1)(C) of the America Invents Act — verify applicability for pre‑AIA patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof Required for Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof Required: More likely than not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution standard for CBM (as contrasted with some other proceedings) is that the petitioner must show unpatentability by a preponderance (more likely than not). Tailor evidentiary showing in the petition to meet this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to File
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM petitions are filed with the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) at the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery scope (comparison to PGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery in CBM: All discovery necessary in interest of justice. (Compared to PGR: Limited to evidence related to arguments asserted in petition.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM proceedings generally permit broader discovery than post-grant review; plan accordingly for document and witness discovery. The breadth may increase cost and timing considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions from the PTAB in CBM proceedings may be appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. Consider appellate strategy when deciding whether to file or settle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical CBM proceedings take roughly 12–18 months from institution to final written decision; factor this timeframe into case planning and client counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects / Remedies if Claims Found Unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PTAB determines that one or more claims of the patent are unpatentable, those claims may be cancelled or amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM provides a mechanism to cancel or require amendment of challenged claims. Use CBM strategically when the goal is claim cancellation or clearing freedom-to-operate issues for financial/ business-method-related patents.
